paper_title: I Don't Know Explicit Modeling of Uncertainty with an [IDK] Token
caption: Average performance on closed-book factual sentence completion benchmarks of models in terms of their parameter count. 70m to 2.8B are , while 7.0B is .
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the average performance (in percentage) of language models on closed-book factual sentence completion benchmarks as a function of model size, which is displayed on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 70 million (70m) to 7.0 billion (7.0B) parameters. The y-axis, labeled “Avg. Performance (%)”, spans from 0 to 80% with major tick marks at intervals of 20%. Three performance metrics are plotted: Precision (red line with upward-pointing triangle markers), Recall (blue line with upward-pointing triangle markers), and F1-score (purple line with upward-pointing triangle markers). Precision starts at approximately 79% for the 70m model and gradually declines to about 74% at 410m, then stabilizes near 75–77% across larger models up to 7.0B. Recall begins at roughly 8% for the 70m model and steadily increases to approximately 44% at 7.0B. The F1-score starts at around 14% for the 70m model, rises to about 32% at 410m, and continues climbing to approximately 56% at 7.0B. All three lines show a generally upward or stable trend with increasing model size, with Recall and F1-score exhibiting more pronounced growth than Precision. The legend in the upper right identifies each metric by color and marker. The caption notes that models from 70m to 2.8B are of one type (implied by context, likely standard models), while the 7.0B model is of another (likely incorporating the [IDK] token mechanism), though the plot itself does not visually distinguish them beyond parameter count.
